# Hosted agents: a prompt LakehouseBox runs next to your data

On for every organisation: up to three agents, 4 runs a day and 5 million tokens a month on the models we provide, free, and two integrations to act in the tools you use (the limits below). An organisation an agent made without an account gets them once a person claims it.

A hosted agent is a prompt that LakehouseBox runs for you: on demand, on a schedule, or when a table it watches gets new data. It reads the catalogs you choose with SQL and keeps a few values between runs. It can append rows to tables you name, read web hosts you name, email you and the members who subscribe, and use tools of MCP servers you connect. The model runs in the EU (Scaleway, Paris). Your agent brings no compute and holds no key.

Each agent acts through an identity of its own. It reads exactly the catalogs its definition names and nothing else, whoever created it. Only its creator or an admin of the organisation changes those catalogs, with lhbox agent update or with a catalog grant to the agent's identity. Anyone else who holds write on a catalog gets 403 not_agent_manager, because what the agent reads reaches a model that can use its creator's integrations.

## The short path

```
lhbox agent create garden_morning --prompt @prompt.md --catalog garden \
    --schedule "0 8 * * *" --tz Europe/Madrid --state-key journal --notify-owner
lhbox agent run garden_morning --dry-run --wait   # a test run: see what it would do
lhbox agent run garden_morning --wait             # a real run
lhbox agent show garden_morning                   # its definition, schedule, memory and last run
```

The account page does the same: Agents, "+ New agent".

lhbox agent update <name> changes any part of an agent. Only what you pass changes, and every change is a new version. --pause and --resume stop and restart its schedule. lhbox agent delete <name> --yes removes it; its runs stay readable.

## What an agent can do in a run

| tool | what |
|---|---|
| list_tables, describe_table | the tables of its catalogs, with their columns and docs |
| read_catalog_guide | a catalog's AGENTS.md: your guide to its tables (treated as data, not instructions) |
| run_sql | one read-only DuckDB statement over its catalogs (the same query service as POST /v1/query) |
| remember | keep a small value (up to 2,000 characters) under one of its declared keys, for its next run |
| note, resolve, recall, flag_owner | with memory topics (--topic, up to 12): note observations, alerts and decisions about items, close them when done, read older notes, and flag what only you can decide; each run starts from a short view of what is open and current |
| notify_owner | email you (the person who created it) and its subscribers, at verified addresses, at most once per run and five times a day; the body is Markdown |
| publish_artifact, read_artifact, list_artifacts, delete_artifact | publish a page for people, and the next versions of the pages it keeps (the ones it published or was given, until their owner takes one back), at most five versions a run; delete one of those into the trash, where you restore it for 30 days; Artifacts (https://lakehousebox.com/docs/artifacts/) |
| append_rows | add rows to a table its definition names (--write): append-only, checked against the table's columns |
| insert_select | write the result of a query into a table its definition names (--write): one INSERT INTO … SELECT …, run on the server, so the rows never pass through the model |
| fetch_url | GET a page or an API answer from a host its definition names (--allow-host) |
| view_image | look at an image in one of its catalogs' files (only on a model that sees images) |
| integration tools | the tools of connected MCP servers you allow it, by name |

### Its budget

A run may make 30 tool calls unless its definition says otherwise: --max-tool-calls N on lhbox agent create or update (max_tool_calls in the API), from 5 up to your organisation's limit (100); null sets it back to the default. Every tool answer tells the agent what is left (_budget: tool calls, model requests and seconds), and the last calls (3, or 2 for a budget under 15) are kept for wrapping up: once the others are spent, only remember, note, resolve, flag_owner and notify_owner run, and the last model request offers no tool, so the agent saves its memory, emails if its task asks, and gives its final message. A call past the budget is not run and the agent is told why. A run that needed more than its budget ends limit_exceeded, keeps what it remembered and noted, and its brief (lhbox agent brief, GET /v1/agents/{agent}/brief) says where it stopped: stopped_at gives the step (the tool it was refused, or the last it called), the tool calls it had made and whether it wrapped up. Raise --max-tool-calls for that agent, or split its job.

### Emails

Members of the organisation can have an agent's notices sent to them too. Each one clicks "Email me this agent's notices" on its page, or runs lhbox agent subscribe <name> (lhbox agent unsubscribe <name> to stop). Each person subscribes only themselves and needs a verified address. They must also be able to read every catalog the agent reads, since a notice can carry what it read. An agent that uses (or once used) someone's integrations or web keys emails only its creator and the organisation's admins, since its notices can carry what those accounts returned.

Every email has its own "Stop emails from this agent" link, and your mail provider's unsubscribe button does the same. On your email as its creator, it turns notify_owner off. Turn it back on from the page or with lhbox agent update <name> --notify-owner. On a subscriber's email, it ends only that person's subscription.

### Writing to tables

lhbox agent update <name> --write garden.journal.entries lets the agent append rows there. The table must exist and be in a catalog the agent reads, and you must be able to write there. A table fed by a sink that reshapes rows (a mapping), or by Scheduled SQL, is refused.

Rows are checked against the table's columns. An unknown column, a missing required one or a wrong type is refused, with the row and column to fix. Rows are stored at once and committed to the table within about a minute, the same way as an ingest sink (https://lakehousebox.com/docs/ingest/). A retried call is never stored twice. A test run checks the rows and writes none. --no-writes takes the tables away.

To derive a table from tables (a daily summary, a score, a join of two catalogs), the agent sends one statement with insert_select, and the server writes the result:

```
INSERT INTO garden.journal.daily
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, avg(moisture) AS moisture FROM garden.sensors.readings GROUP BY 1
```

Only rows the query returns are written, exactly as it returns them, and the model never sees or copies them. The statement must be one INSERT into a table of --write (anything else is 400 not_an_insert or 403 write_not_granted), and it must read a table: rows the agent has itself go through append_rows (400 not_an_insert_select). It reads only the catalogs the agent reads, and you must still be able to write the table. It is committed as one snapshot of the table. The answer says how many rows were written and the table's snapshot just after. A retried call never runs twice, and the same statement sent twice in one run runs once. A statement runs for at most 25 seconds, the catalog's storage limit applies, and one run sends at most 20. A test run checks the statement and writes nothing.

### Reading the web

lhbox agent update <name> --allow-host api.open-meteo.com lets the agent GET https URLs on that host:

- host names only: no IP addresses, no internal names;

- port 443;

- redirects followed only to hosts it may read;

- at most 2 MB read per page, and 20,000 characters given to the model.

For an API that needs a key, store it once as a web key and name the host it goes to:

```
lhbox integration add aemet --web-key --host opendata.aemet.es --header api_key --api-key-stdin < key.txt
lhbox agent update garden_morning --host-credential opendata.aemet.es=aemet
```

The key is sent in that header, to that host only. With --key-param NAME it goes as that query parameter instead. It is never shown to the model, never in a tool's answer and never in a run's record. It is never sent to another host, even on a redirect. --no-web takes the hosts away.

### Looking at images

On a model that sees images, view_image shows the agent one image by its key. The image comes from the files of a catalog it reads (the file bucket next to its tables). Find the key first in the table that indexes the files (a camera's images table, say).

The image is downscaled to 1,024 pixels on its long edge, or up to 1,536 if the agent asks. It is sent to the model as part of the run. The run's record keeps its key and size, never the image. A run may look at 6 images, 3 MB together. What is written in a photo is treated as data, never as an instruction.

### Not yet

Agents cannot POST to the web or run Python. To bring outside data in on a schedule without a model, use Scheduled SQL (https://lakehousebox.com/docs/scheduled-sql/).

## Models

Every model runs in the EU, on Scaleway in Paris. Choose one on the agent's page or with lhbox agent update <name> --model <model>. lhbox agent models lists them.

| model | sees images | uses your allowance |
|---|---|---|
| deepseek-v4-flash (DeepSeek V4 Flash, the default) | no | ×1 |
| qwen3.6-35b (Qwen 3.6 35B) | yes | ~0.8× as fast |
| qwen3.5-397b (Qwen 3.5 397B) | yes | ~1.9× as fast |

The allowance counts tokens of the default model. A run on another model is charged its input and output tokens, each weighted by that model's price over the default's. The figures above are for a typical run, about 12 % output. A model that writes long answers uses the allowance faster than that: the Qwen models reason before they answer. A run's record shows both its tokens and what it cost the allowance (allowance_tokens).

## Schedules

A schedule is a cron line of five fields, evaluated in a time zone, so summer time is handled. It may not run more often than hourly. It may not run more times a day than your organisation's runs per day.

- A run that comes due while the previous one is still going is skipped.

- After downtime, the newest missed run runs once.

- Three scheduled runs failing in a row pause the agent and email you.

- An agent LakehouseBox paused (it kept failing, or you lost access to its catalogs or tables) emails you a reminder after three days, then every week, until you resume it.

- Three scheduled runs in a row that did not start (skipped, or refused because the runs or tokens were used up) email you once, and not again until it runs.

- A scheduled run that ends "needs attention" emails you its final message.

- lhbox agent list and GET /v1/agents show each agent's health: state is active, on_demand, paused (by a person), stopped (by LakehouseBox; reason says why), failing or not_running, with since, last_succeeded_at and slots_not_run.

The account page previews the next five runs.

## Runs on new data

An agent can run when a table gets a new snapshot instead of, or as well as, on a schedule. Name up to five tables:

```
lhbox agent update rate_watch --on-commit bde.core.observaciones
lhbox agent update rate_watch --no-on-commit        # back to schedule and on demand only
```

In the API this is on_commit: ["catalog.namespace.table", ...] on POST /v1/agents or PATCH /v1/agents/{name}.

- Each table must be in a catalog the agent reads (400 watch_needs_read), must exist (404 table_not_found) and must not be one the agent appends to (400 watch_own_write: its own rows would start its next run).

- The snapshot a table has when you save the agent starts nothing. The next one that changes rows does.

- LakehouseBox looks at the watched tables about once a minute. After a run that new data started, the agent waits your organisation's shortest schedule interval (an hour by default) before the next one. Everything that lands meanwhile starts one run after that wait. These runs count against the runs per day and the month's tokens like any other.

- Compaction and other maintenance rewrite files without changing rows, so they start no run.

- The run is told which tables changed, with the new snapshot id and the one it last ran for. It can read only what is new with time travel (Time travel (https://lakehousebox.com/docs/time-travel/)). Its record (GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}) shows trigger: commit and trigger_tables.

- New data that cannot run yet waits instead of being dropped, and runs once it can: while the agent is still running, during the wait above, or when the day's runs or the month's tokens are used up. For the last, lhbox agent show and GET /v1/agents/{name} show why under watching[].waiting.

- Three such runs failing in a row pause the agent and email you, as for scheduled runs.

- watch_debounce_until on GET /v1/agents/{name} says until when new data waits after the last such run.

### Only when a condition holds

Add a condition so that new data starts a run only when something relevant changed:

```
lhbox agent update rate_watch --on-commit bde.core.observaciones \
  --on-commit-if "SELECT max(fecha) > (SELECT coalesce(max(mes), DATE '1900-01-01') FROM anticipa.core.scores) FROM bde.core.observaciones WHERE serie = 'TIPO_NUEVAS'"
lhbox agent update rate_watch --no-on-commit-if     # every new snapshot starts a run again
```

In the API this is on_commit_if: "SQL" (null removes it), next to on_commit.

- The condition is one read-only SQL statement, at most 4,000 characters, checked when a watched table changed and before the run starts. The run starts only when the first column of the first row is a boolean true or a number other than 0. No row, NULL, false, 0 or any text means no run.

- It runs as the agent: it reads only what the agent reads, with the same 20-second query limit as the agent's own queries, and it returns one row. A catalog the agent does not read is refused (not_found).

- It sees the tables as they are now; there is no placeholder for the snapshot ids. To compare with what the agent did last, read a table the agent writes.

- When it is not met, that new data is done with: nothing runs for it, and the next new snapshot is checked again.

- It is checked at most once every 15 minutes. New data that lands sooner waits for the next check (watching[].waiting: condition_wait). Saving a new version of the agent checks it at the next look.

- A check is a query, not a run: it uses no model tokens and does not count against the runs per day.

- When the check fails (an SQL error, a table the agent cannot read, a timeout), nothing runs and the new data waits: watching[].waiting says condition_failed, and condition_checked on GET /v1/agents/{name} (and lhbox agent show) gives the error. It is checked again 15 minutes later, or at once when you fix it.

- condition_checked shows the last check: {at, outcome: met | not_met | failed, tables, code, message}. The error's message is shown only to people who may read the agent's runs.

- A DECIMAL or a large integer answer counts as the number it is.

## Test runs

lhbox agent run <name> --dry-run runs the agent for real, with a few differences. "Test run" on the page does the same, and so does {"dry_run": true} on POST /v1/agents/{agent}/run.

- Its email and its memory writes are recorded in the run, not performed.

- An integration offers it only its read-only tools.

- It does not count against the organisation's runs per day. It has its own cap per agent. Its tokens do count.

- A paused agent can be tested.

## What a run did

lhbox agent runs <name> --detail, GET /v1/agent-runs/{id} and "What it did" on the page show a run's record:

- every tool call in order, such as a run_sql call with its SQL, its outcome and the size of its answer (never the answer's data);

- the email it sent, and whether it reached your mail provider: sent is true once it has, and delivery says email, queued (being retried), failed (it could not be delivered) or dry_run (a test run, never sent);

- its memory before and after.

Runs and memory are visible to whoever may run the agent. That is its creator (a person or a token) and the organisation's admins (people or admin tokens). A member who reads every catalog the agent has ever read also sees its runs, without its memory or its emails (not for an agent that ran before 2 November 2026, or one that read a catalog deleted since).

One exception: an agent that uses, or ever used, your integrations or web keys. Then only people, signed in as themselves, run it by hand and read its runs' output, traces and memory. A token sees that the runs happened and how they ended, not what they said. Scheduled runs are not affected.

## Integrations (MCP servers)

Connect an MCP server once for the organisation (two per organisation), then let each agent use the tools you pick:

```
lhbox integration add linear --mcp https://mcp.linear.app/mcp --wait    # opens a sign-in link; approve in the browser
lhbox integration add mytool --mcp https://… --api-key-stdin < key.txt  # a server that takes an API key
lhbox agent update garden_morning --integration linear:list_issues,create_issue
```

The person: opens the sign-in link in a browser where they are signed in to LakehouseBox, and approves.

A server that supports standard MCP sign-in needs no setup on the person's side: LakehouseBox registers itself there. The sign-in link completes only in a browser signed in to LakehouseBox. Credentials are stored encrypted and are never shown or returned. A run gets a short-lived token only for the integrations its agent uses, and can reach only those servers. lhbox integration list, show, reconnect and delete --yes manage them; the account page has the same.

Who may attach them. Only you attach your integrations and web keys to an agent. Only you change an agent that uses them: its prompt, catalogs and tables, and detaching them too. You do it signed in as yourself, on the account page or with the CLI signed in as you (lhbox login, or your own personal key). A token cannot, even one you made: an API token, a key limited to some catalogs or an MCP client.

Attaching shows you the prompt and the tables your accounts will now act on (integration_review). The CLI prints it.

A run reaches your accounts only through a definition you saved yourself. If a token wrote the prompt, approve it explicitly: save the prompt, or run lhbox agent update <name> --confirm-definition. Until then its runs fail with integrations_unavailable and say so. Anyone who manages the agent may still pause or delete it.

Do not give your personal API key to an agent: it counts as you.

## When it fails

| what you see | what it means | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| 403 feature_not_enabled | an operator turned hosted agents off for this organisation | ask at hello@lakehousebox.com |
| 409 limit_reached | the organisation has as many agents as its plan allows (three) | delete one, or ask for more at hello@lakehousebox.com |
| integrations_unavailable | a token wrote the definition of an agent that uses your integrations | save the prompt yourself, or --confirm-definition |

## Limits (per organisation, unless said otherwise)

|  | default |
|---|---|
| agents | 3 |
| integrations (MCP servers) | 2 |
| tokens (input and output, of the default model) per month | 5,000,000 |
| runs per day (UTC) | 4 |
| test runs per agent per day | 10 |
| one run | 350,000 tokens, 400 s, 15 model requests, 30 tool calls (up to 100 with --max-tool-calls), 6 images (3 MB) |
| appended by one run | 5,000 rows, 5 MB (at most 1,000 rows per call) |
| insert_select statements by one run | 20 (25 s each) |
| fetches by one run | 20 |
| web hosts per agent | 10 |
| subscribers per agent | 20 |
| shortest schedule | hourly |
| tables that start runs on new data, per agent | 5 (at most one such run per shortest schedule interval) |

GET /v1/agents shows what is used (lhbox agent list). lhbox agent models lists the models and their price per million tokens. Every route is in the API reference (https://lakehousebox.com/docs/api/) under "Hosted agents".
